- **Breaking:** Requires `a2ui_core` `^0.7.0` (`a2ui_cli` exposes `a2ui_core`
  types in its public API).

- Added `a2ui lint` (`LintCommand`, `lintCatalog`, `CatalogLintFinding`, and `LintSeverity`) to validate catalog JSON schemas against deterministic protocol rules with JSON Pointer locations, including v1.0 Unicode UAX 31 identifiers, component and function discriminators, the reserved `Surface` component name, v1.0 `requiresUserActivation` caller constraints, and redundant `ComponentCommon` or `FunctionCommon` wrapping ([#3831](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/pull/3831)).

detail.readme: # A2UI **Build delightful, fast, reliable agentic experiences** A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open-source generative UI framework, complete with a protocol optimized for streaming dynamic user interfaces at low latency, native renderers for web and mobile frameworks, and agent SDKs in several popular languages. With A2UI, your agents can communicate with your users using natively rendered widgets, in addition to text. _Examples of UI compositions that A2UI can express._ ## Quick links - [Main website](https://a2ui.org). - Try it in your browser using [A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/). - [Supported renderers](https://a2ui.org/reference/renderers/). - [Supported agents](https://a2ui.org/reference/agents/). - [Protocol specification](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/). ## Introduction Large language models (LLMs) and decision models (e.g. [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/)) excel at creating text and code and at making fast decisions on top of raw structured data (e.g. JSON). A2UI gives these models a specialized vocabulary for expressing user interfaces. A2UI expresses UI using _data_, not code. A schema for the data exchanged between the agent and the renderer enforces strict capability boundaries for the agent, keeping agent-generated experiences safe and aligned with the business requirements of your application. A _core library_, a _native framework adapter_, and a _catalog of components_ provide access to native components and form the building blocks that the agent _composes_ into a final user experience, making the result expressive and high-performance. ## When to use A2UI Use A2UI when any of the following apply to your application: - Parts of your application are agent- and/or server-driven. By design, A2UI supports remote rendering. - You want the UI to be composed dynamically, tailored to the user's immediate need. Instead of making your users navigate through multiple screens to solve their problems, have the agent build the right flow of UI that guides users directly to solutions. - You need the highest performance and visual fidelity. A2UI renders UI using the framework of your choice, typically one that the host app itself is written in. WebViews or HTML are not required. - The same agent streams UI to multiple platforms or frameworks, such as Flutter, React, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. A2UI helps keep the user experience compatible and consistent across all screens. - The agent is remote, third-party, or operates across a trust boundary. For example, the agent must not be able to handle certain kinds of data (credit card/account numbers, PII, financial data). A2UI helps enforce the trust boundary and protect your app's critical functionality from hallucinations using a strict schema, and by expressing UI using validated data rather than executable code. ## A2UI core philosophy We develop A2UI under the guidance of the following core principles: - **Security first**: The app developer controls what the agent can and cannot do in the app. A2UI provides a framework for specifying and enforcing the necessary guardrails, such as expressing UI as data, validating inputs and outputs against a schema, and disallowing arbitrary executable code. Every capability granted to the agent is either a safe standard capability built into the framework, or a capability explicitly granted by the app developer. - **Model-friendly and server-driven**: The A2UI protocol is designed to be efficiently generated by language and decision models and transported over the network, and to support progressive rendering (or "streaming") for a responsive user experience. An agent can adapt the UI based on where the user takes the conversation. A2UI supports swappable inference formats, so you can tailor inference to specific models and use cases. - **Native rendering and portability**: A2UI renders UI using the framework native to your app, with renderers for many major UI frameworks. No need to change frameworks unless required for other reasons. ## Architecture A2UI's architecture is made of multiple layers spanning the full stack that connects the agent to the application: 1. **Inference**: An agent (typically backed by a language or a decision model) instructed by an A2UI skill (created using an A2UI Agent SDK) generates the description of UI and data using an appropriate inference format (e.g. A2UI Express, or a decision tree). 2. **Transport**: An A2UI Agent SDK, embedded in a larger agent architecture, parses and validates the model's output, expands macros, and converts the UI to the wire-stable _A2UI Transport_ protocol messages, which are sent to the renderer. 3. **Rendering**: A renderer is made of an _A2UI Core_ library (e.g. the `@a2ui/web_core` npm package, or `a2ui_core` Dart package), a UI framework adapter (e.g. `@a2ui/react` React adapter, or `a2ui_flutter` Flutter adapter), and a widget catalog. The core library parses the incoming messages and creates a framework-agnostic in-memory representation of the UI and data. The framework adapter maps the in-memory representation to concrete framework-specific UI widgets. The widget catalog provides access to the widgets the agent is allowed to compose. ## Getting started Pick the path that matches where you want to start: | Path | What you get | Time | | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | | 🍜 **[Quickstart](https://a2ui.org/quickstart/)** | A full-stack A2UI app with a backend and frontend. Learn A2UI end-to-end and customize to your use case. | ~5 min | | 🎨 **[A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/)** | Generate A2UI JSON from a visual editor and paste it into any agent prompt — no install required. | ~1 min | | 🎬 **[A2UI Theater](https://a2ui-composer.ag-ui.com/theater)** | Step through pre-built A2UI streaming scenarios across Lit, React, and Angular renderers — no install required. | ~1 min | ## Packages These packages are developed in this repository. cross-framework templating engine and a set of standard primitives for rendering reusable rich UI widgets. - **Sandboxed logic**: A way to securely attach logic to A2UI components. - **Agent SDK**: Skill generation, better diagnostics, and integrations with more agent frameworks. - **Evals**: A set of tools for evaluating generated UI quality. - **MCP Apps**: Embedding MCP Apps inside A2UI, and embedding A2UI experiences into MCP Apps. - **CLI**: Schema validation, codegen, local preview, and integration with coding agents. ## Contribute A2UI is an **Apache 2.0** licensed project. We believe the future of UI is agentic, and we want to work with you to help build it. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details on how to get started.
